articleBody:
A successful bathroom painting project depends entirely on thorough surface preparation and proper drying conditions. High humidity, leftover soap residue, and concealed water damage can ruin new paint quickly if they are not addressed before the brushes come out. Use this checklist to confirm your room is ready for a long-lasting, moisture-resistant finish.

- [ ] Inspect existing drywall and plaster for soft spots — Spongy or crumbling wallboard indicates active leaks that must be repaired before applying any primer.
- [ ] Check older coatings for potential lead paint — Homes built before 1978 require lead-safe preparation techniques before scraping or sanding old layers.
- [ ] Clean walls with a degreaser to remove soap film — Bath oils and body residues prevent fresh coatings from bonding securely to the wall surface.
- [ ] Scrape away all peeling, blistered, or loose paint — New coatings will pull away from the wall if applied directly over unstable, flaking layers.
- [ ] Treat and remove active mildew spots completely — Painting over living mold spores allows mildew to grow straight through your new finish.
- [ ] Strip out moldy or cracked caulk around tubs and vanities — Fresh, flexible sealant must be installed after painting to keep water out of wall cavities.
- [ ] Sand glossy enamel surfaces to create mechanical grip — Dull down slick existing trim and walls so your new primer adheres tightly.
- [ ] Confirm the bathroom exhaust fan vents directly outdoors — Proper exhaust ventilation prevents humidity from lingering on freshly applied coatings.
- [ ] Clear off countertops and remove hanging hardware — Keeping fixtures, mirrors, and switch plates out of the way ensures crisp, clean lines.
- [ ] Plan for 48 to 72 hours of continued ventilation — Following EPA guidelines for indoor air quality and cure times protects the finish from moisture damage.

How to Use This Checklist:
Review these items with your remodeling team before work begins.
